topic: Triangles — properties and theorems — mixed tiers
description: Angle sum, exterior angle, Pythagoras, similarity criteria, area

questions.stem: In a triangle, two angles are 55° and 65°. The third angle is:
questions.explanation: Angle sum property of a triangle: the three interior angles always add up to 180°. So third angle = 180 − 55 − 65 = 60°. Verify: 55 + 65 + 60 = 180 ✓.

questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, the legs are 9 cm and 12 cm. The hypotenuse is:
questions.explanation: Pythagoras' theorem: hyp² = leg₁² + leg₂² = 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225. Hyp = √225 = 15 cm. The 9-12-15 triple is a 3× scaling of the classic 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple. Memorise key triples: (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17), (7,24,25).

questions.stem: An exterior angle of a triangle is 110°. The two interior opposite angles add up to:
questions.explanation: Exterior Angle Theorem: an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior opposite (non-adjacent) angles. So sum = 110°. Quick proof — exterior + adjacent interior = 180° (linear pair); all three interior angles = 180°; subtract → exterior = sum of remote interior angles.

questions.stem: The area of an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm is:
questions.explanation: Area of an equilateral triangle = (√3 / 4) · a², where a = side. Here a = 6, so area = (√3 / 4) · 36 = 9√3 cm². Numerical value ≈ 9 × 1.732 = 15.59 cm². Companion formula: height = (√3/2) · a; perimeter = 3a; in-radius = a/(2√3); circum-radius = a/√3.

questions.stem: In two similar triangles, the ratio of corresponding sides is 3 : 5. The ratio of their areas is:
questions.explanation: For similar figures, ratio of areas = (ratio of corresponding lengths)². So area ratio = 3² : 5² = 9 : 25. Companion: ratio of perimeters = ratio of sides = 3:5; ratio of volumes (for similar solids) = (3:5)³ = 27 : 125.

questions.stem: In a triangle ABC, the medians from A, B and C meet at a single point called the:
questions.explanation: Centroid (G) — intersection of medians (lines from vertex to midpoint of opposite side). Divides each median in 2:1 ratio (vertex side : midpoint side). Other 'centres': Incentre (I) — meeting of angle bisectors, equidistant from sides; Orthocentre (H) — meeting of altitudes; Circumcentre (O) — meeting of perpendicular bisectors of sides, equidistant from vertices. Euler's line — H, G, O are collinear (G is 1/3 of the way from O to H).

questions.stem: In ΔABC, the sides are AB = 5, BC = 12, CA = 13. The triangle is:
questions.explanation: Test for right angle: square the longest side and check if it equals sum of squares of the other two. 13² = 169; 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 ✓. So Pythagoras holds — triangle is right-angled. The right angle is opposite the longest side (hypotenuse = AC = 13), so the right angle is at vertex B. (5, 12, 13) is a primitive Pythagorean triple.
